instruction: Open the main settings page in Chrome to view all configuration options.

metadata.explanation: Task requires the agent to navigate to Chrome's main settings page. The evaluator checks if the active tab URL matches chrome://settings/. Uses existing is_expected_active_tab_approximate metric and get_active_url_from_accessTree getter.
metadata.verification: Reusing existing framework functions - no new functions needed. The task follows the same pattern as the original but navigates to a different settings page.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator can correctly verify that user navigated to Chrome settings page
Getter 'get_active_url_from_accessTree' correctly extracts active tab URL from accessibility tree
Metric 'is_expected_active_tab_approximate' correctly compares URLs by stripping query parameters
Expected URL 'chrome://settings/' is semantically correct for Chrome main settings
Data flow is correct: getter extracts URL string → metric compares against expected

Minor over-permissiveness: metric accepts any settings subpage (e.g., chrome://settings/privacy) due to query parameter stripping, while instruction specifies 'main settings page where all configuration options are displayed' which implies root page only
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider using 'is_expected_active_tab' (exact match) instead of 'is_expected_active_tab_approximate' if strict root settings page verification is required
Current implementation will accept chrome://settings/privacy or chrome://settings/appearance as valid, which may be more permissive than intended
